bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation at risk for stroke, dabigatran 150 mg twice daily reduced stroke or systemic embolism versus warfarin (relative risk, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82).
implications: These results support that, in this trial, dabigatran 150 mg twice daily had lower annual rates of stroke or systemic embolism than warfarin (1.11% per year vs 1.69% per year; relative risk, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82) with similar major bleeding (3.11% per year vs 3.36% per year; P = 0.31), while dabigatran 110 mg twice daily had similar stroke or systemic embolism (1.53% per year vs 1.69% per year; relative risk, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.11) and lower major bleeding (2.71% per year vs 3.36% per year; P = 0.003). The document also reports higher myocardial infarction rates with dabigatran than with warfarin and does not establish differences in mortality at conventional significance levels (e.g., P = 0.051 for dabigatran 150 mg vs warfarin).

major_points.text: Randomized noninferiority trial comparing two fixed doses of dabigatran (blinded) with warfarin (unblinded).
major_points.quote: In this noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned 18,113 patients who had atrial fi- brillation and a risk of stroke to receive, in a blinded fashion, fixed doses of dab- igatran — 110 mg or 150 mg twice daily — or, in an unblinded fashion, adjusted-dose warfarin.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was stroke or systemic embolism; median follow-up was 2.0 years.
major_points.quote: The median duration of the follow-up period was 2.0 years. The primary outcome was stroke or systemic embolism.

major_points.text: Dabigatran 150 mg twice daily was superior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism.
major_points.quote: Rates of the primary outcome were 1.69% per year in the warfarin group... and 1.11% per year in the group that received 150 mg of dabigatran (relative risk, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82; P<0.001 for superiority).

major_points.text: Dabigatran 110 mg twice daily was noninferior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism.
major_points.quote: Rates of the primary outcome were 1.69% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 1.53% per year in the group that received 110 mg of dabigatran (relative risk with dabigatran, 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 1.11;

major_points.text: Major bleeding was lower with dabigatran 110 mg vs warfarin, but similar with dabigatran 150 mg vs warfarin.
major_points.quote: The rate of major bleeding was 3.36% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 2.71% per year in the group receiving 110 mg of dabigatran (P = 0.003) and 3.11% per year in the group receiving 150 mg of dabigatran (P = 0.31).

major_points.text: Hemorrhagic stroke occurred less often with dabigatran (both doses) than with warfarin.
major_points.quote: The rate of hemorrhagic stroke was 0.38% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 0.12% per year with 110 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001) and 0.10% per year with 150 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001).

criticisms.text: Open-label warfarin could have introduced bias in reporting or adjudication of events.
criticisms.quote: The use of open-label warfarin could have in- troduced a bias in the reporting or adjudication of events.

criticisms.text: A dose-tailoring concept was not specifically tested in the trial.
criticisms.quote: These findings suggest that the dose of dabigatran could potentially be tailored to take into consideration the risk characteristics of a spe- cific patient, although this concept was not spe- cifically tested in our trial.

criticisms.text: The explanation for higher myocardial infarction rates with dabigatran than warfarin was uncertain.
